_comment: Frozen claims for measuring the VERIFIER, not the answer generator.
Every claim is written against the real stored text of the cited section,
so the label is checkable by reading that section rather than by trusting
whoever wrote the row. Answers are not generated at eval time: the only
variable is the verifier, which makes the run deterministic in its inputs
and cheap to repeat across the model chain.
expected_verdict is what a correct verifier must return.
expected_stage, where given, is which stage must reach it -- a claim
settled by a string comparison must not cost a model call.

cases.claim: A promoter who fails to give possession by the agreed date is liable, on demand, to return the amount received from an allottee who wishes to withdraw.
cases.note: restates s.18(1) directly

cases.claim: An allottee is entitled to obtain information about sanctioned plans and layout plans approved by the competent authority.
An allottee is entitled to know the stage-wise time schedule for completion of the project.
A transgender person may apply to the District Magistrate for a certificate of identity.
Where the applicant is a minor child, the application for a certificate of identity must be made by a parent or guardian.
An order for payment of money made by the Registrar of Copyrights is deemed to be a decree of a civil court and is executable in the same manner.
cases.note: label corrected 2026-08-28: s.75 deems the order a decree only "on a certificate issued by" the Registrar. The claim drops that condition, so it overstates. The verifier called this consistently across both runs and was right.

cases.claim: The Central Government may, by order in writing, require a person to furnish information in his possession relating to property against which action is proposed under the Act.
A deposit taker whose property is about to be attached may apply to the Designated Court to deposit the fair value of the property in lieu of attachment.
An application to deposit fair value in lieu of attachment must be made before the attachment is confirmed.
The State Government is required to cause a register of pharmacists to be prepared for the State.
The register of pharmacists must include the full name and residential address of each registered person.
Officers and employees of the Commission are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code when acting under the Act.
The Chairperson of the Centre is appointed by the Central Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
Every copyright society must publish its tariff scheme in the prescribed manner.
An offence under the Act is compoundable at the instance of the married Muslim woman upon whom talaq is pronounced.
cases.note: label corrected 2026-08-28: s.7(b) makes compounding subject to the permission of the Magistrate. The claim drops that, so it overstates.

cases.claim: A promoter who misses the possession date must refund the allottee automatically, without any demand being made.
cases.note: s.18 says 'liable on demand'; removing the demand overstates it

cases.claim: A promoter who misses the possession date must refund every allottee in the project.
cases.note: only an allottee who wishes to withdraw

cases.claim: Any person may apply to the District Magistrate for a transgender certificate of identity on behalf of a minor.
cases.note: a parent or guardian, not any person

cases.claim: The Central Government may require any person to furnish any information it wants.
cases.note: limited to property against which action is proposed

cases.claim: A deposit taker may deposit the fair value of the property in lieu of attachment at any time.
cases.note: only before confirmation of attachment

cases.claim: An order of the Registrar of Copyrights is a decree of a civil court for every purpose under the Act.
cases.note: orders for payment of money only

cases.claim: The Chairperson of the Centre must be a former Judge of the Supreme Court.
cases.note: a High Court judge or an eminent person also qualify

cases.claim: Every offence under the Act is cognizable.
cases.note: cognizable only if information is given by the woman or a relative

cases.claim: The State Council prepares the register of pharmacists for the State.
cases.note: the State Government prepares it; the Council maintains it

cases.claim: Anyone aggrieved by a copyright society's tariff scheme may appeal without paying anything.
cases.note: the proviso requires fees already due to be paid

cases.claim: A promoter who fails to give possession on time is liable to imprisonment for up to three years.
cases.note: s.18 creates a monetary liability, not an offence

cases.claim: An allottee may take physical possession of the project office if the promoter defaults.
A transgender person is entitled to reservation in public employment.
cases.note: s.5 is about applying for a certificate of identity

cases.claim: The District Magistrate must decide a certificate of identity application within thirty days.
cases.note: no time limit appears in s.5

cases.claim: A person who fails to furnish information commits an offence punishable with fine.
cases.note: s.21 confers a power; it prescribes no penalty

cases.claim: The Designated Court must refund the deposit with interest if the attachment is later set aside.
A pharmacist removed from the register may appeal to the High Court.
cases.note: s.29 concerns preparation of the register

cases.claim: Members of the Commission are immune from prosecution for acts done under the Act.
cases.note: being a public servant is not immunity; it is the opposite

cases.claim: The Centre must consist of at least seven members.
A copyright society that fails to publish its tariff scheme may be wound up by the Central Government.
Talaq-e-biddat is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to seven years.
cases.note: s.7 is procedural; the punishment is elsewhere in the Act

cases.claim: An order of the Appellate Board may be appealed directly to the Supreme Court.
cases.note: s.75 mentions the High Court

cases.claim: Section 18 makes the promoter "liable on demand to the allottees, in case the allottee wishes to withdraw from the project".
cases.note: verbatim; a string comparison settles it with no model call

cases.claim: Section 5 provides that an application may be made "to the District Magistrate for issuing a certificate of identity as a transgender person".
Section 52 says officers shall be "deemed, when acting or purporting to act in pursuance of any of the provisions of this Act, to be public servants".
Section 18 provides that the promoter "shall forfeit the entire project and surrender every licence to the authority forthwith".
cases.note: the Delhi HC failure: real section, invented words

cases.claim: Section 5 states that "the District Magistrate shall decide every such application within a period of thirty days".
Section 21 provides that "any person refusing to furnish information shall be punished with imprisonment for a term of one year".
The Act requires a promoter to maintain a separate escrow account.
cases.note: fabricated id: a gap in our shelf, not a finding against the claim

cases.claim: Indian law recognises the doctrine of frustration of contract.
cases.note: cites nothing: a defect in the claim itself

cases.claim: A promoter must refund the allottee with interest.
cases.note: one real id and one invented; the invented one still taints it

cases.claim: An allottee who withdraws is entitled both to a refund from the promoter and to information about the sanctioned plans.
cases.note: each half is supported by one of the two cited sections

cases.claim: An allottee who withdraws is entitled to a refund and to compensation for mental agony.
cases.note: the refund is supported; mental agony is not mentioned

cases.claim: A contract without consideration is void.
cases.note: true in Indian law, absent from the cited text -- the check must judge the text, not recall the law

cases.claim: The Indian Penal Code defines a public servant.
cases.note: s.52 refers to IPC s.21 but does not itself define the term
